heard: A minor planet, barely 155 miles wide, is wearing icy rings. For centuries, rings were only confirmed around giant planets— Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. In 2013, Brazilian astronomer Felipe Braga-Ribas watched the Centaur Chariclo pass in front of a star. The starlight blinked briefly seconds before and after the rock passed, revealing two distinct rings. Down from planetary scales, These rings orbit only about 400 kilometers from Chariklo's center. Even wilder, the two icy bands measure just 7 kilometers and 3 kilometers wide. That solved an old mystery. Chariklo dimmed for a decade when its rings tilted edge onto Earth. Astronomers hypothesize unseen shepherd moons keep them stable, preserving an impossible sight.
